title: Structured `confirm.message` outranks `confirmText` in ActionRunner but has no translation-bundle key — and the types deprecate authors INTO it
body:
Observation found while fixing #4265 (PR #4313). **Dormant today** — nothing in this repo authors the structured form, so no user hits it. Filing so the trap is on record rather than rediscovered later.

## What

`ActionRunner` picks the confirm body with a precedence, not a union:

```ts
// packages/core/src/actions/ActionRunner.ts:896
const confirmMessage = action.confirm?.message || action.confirmText;
```

The translation channel only knows the second one. The bundle convention is
`{ns}.objects.{obj}._actions.{name}.confirmText` (`useObjectLabel().actionConfirm`),
and after #4265 every action-rendering surface resolves that key through one
shared resolver. There is no key for `confirm.message` anywhere.

So an action that declares the structured form gets a confirm dialog whose body
**cannot be translated** — and worse, it does so *silently*: a bundle entry
spelling `confirmText` still resolves, is still written onto the def, and is
then simply outranked by the untranslated `confirm.message`. The failure looks
exactly like #4265 from the outside, with the opposite cause.

## The part that makes it likelier over time

`@object-ui/types` currently points authors AT the untranslatable form:

```ts
// packages/types/src/crud.ts:160
/** @deprecated Use confirm.message instead */
confirmText?: string;
```

That is backwards relative to where the platform actually landed:
`@objectstack/spec`'s action surface carries `confirmText`, the TranslationBundle
carries `confirmText`, and `ActionDef.confirmText` in `packages/types/src/ui-action.ts`
carries no deprecation. An author who follows the `@deprecated` note writes the
one spelling that loses localization.

## Why observation-class, not a defect

Repo-wide grep for an authored `confirm: { … }` on an action turns up nothing
outside type declarations and the runner's own read — only `confirmText` is
produced. Nothing a user can reach today is broken.

## Two candidate dispositions (for triage, not decided here)

1. **Retire the structured arm** — if `confirm: { title, message, confirmText, cancelText }`
   has no business pull, ADR-0049 enforce-or-remove applies, and the contradictory
   `@deprecated` note in `crud.ts` goes with it. One spelling, contract-first.
2. **Give it a bundle key** — keep the arm and resolve `confirm.message` /
   `confirm.title` / the two button labels through the same `_actions` node, so
   declared equals enforced on both arms.

Direction 1 looks right on the startup-focus axis (a declared-but-unconsumed
capability surface earning a second translation vocabulary is exactly the
expansion that needs real pull first), but it is a contract call, so it is the
maintainer's rather than mine.
